nodes.label: fig:ladder — Rolling-Origin Forecast Ladder (three venues, three panels)
nodes.rationale: Small-multiple ranked-dispersion figure replacing tab:ladder. Nine model rungs are ranked worst-at-top within each of three venue panels (Beer Hall, Two River Taps, Ellel) so the reader's eye falls downward onto the retained set. Per rung: a faint 5-95 percentile whisker, a shaded IQR box, a coloured median rule, and a diamond mean drawn as a SEPARATE mark. Red/inked rungs are MCS-retained at alpha=0.10; grey rungs are eliminated. Bars are deliberately NOT bolded by rank because no ranking change between the two rulers survives its own standard error — the retained SET, not the ordering, is the honest object.

nodes.label: Per-Venue Axis (small multiples, no shared scale)
nodes.rationale: Gate-2 ruled Ellel 'unscaled', so its x-axis is RMSE in currency (£, 0-1000) while Beer Hall and Two River Taps are RMSSE on calendar_lag7_active (0-1.5 / 0-1.3). Giving each venue its own axis makes the cross-venue comparison the ruling forbids visually impossible, rather than merely discouraged.

nodes.label: Mean Drawn Outside the Box as the Skew Finding
nodes.rationale: At Ellel the standard deviation exceeds the mean at every rung; the fold-loss distribution is right-skewed and zero-inflated — the occurrence structure that motivated the hurdle model. A mean column in a table would assert a symmetric summary the data does not have, so the box carries median+IQR and the mean is a diamond free to sit outside it. The visible displacement IS the finding, not a rendering flaw.

nodes.label: MCS Membership at alpha=0.10 (what the ink marks)
nodes.rationale: Colour encodes Model Confidence Set membership, not rank. Retained sets differ by venue: Beer Hall retains 5 (Chronos-Bolt, Chronos-2+exo, ETS, Chronos-2, robust DOW); Two River Taps retains 4 (Chronos-2, Chronos-2+exo, Chronos-Bolt, ETS); Ellel retains 6 (Chronos-Bolt, robust DOW, Chronos-2+exo, Chronos-2, STL, ETS). Foundation models and cheap seasonal baselines co-inhabit every retained set — no rung is separable from the others by its own standard error.

nodes.label: Nine-Rung Model Ladder (rung0 naive → rung4 foundation)
nodes.rationale: An ascending-cost ladder: rung0 seasonal naive; rung1 robust DOW; rung2 ETS and STL; rung3 GBM and global GBM; rung4 Chronos-2, Chronos-2+exo, Chronos-Bolt. The figure's purpose is to test whether climbing the ladder buys accuracy — and the answer read off the panels is that it mostly does not.

nodes.label: Beer Hall Panel (RMSSE, calendar_lag7_active, n=273 folds)
nodes.rationale: Largest fold count. Five retained rungs; GBM variants and seasonal naive eliminated. Medians cluster tightly around 0.5-0.7 RMSSE, so the whole ladder occupies a narrow band.

nodes.label: Two River Taps Panel (RMSSE, calendar_lag7_active, n=205 folds)
nodes.rationale: Tightest retained set of the three (4 rungs), all Chronos variants plus ETS. Notably robust DOW is eliminated here while it is retained at both other venues — the retained set is venue-specific, not a global ranking.

nodes.label: Ellel Panel (RMSE in £, unscaled basis, n=260 folds)
nodes.rationale: The unscaled venue: losses are currency MAE/RMSE on a 0-1000 axis. Widest dispersion and the clearest mean-outside-box displacement, and the largest retained set (6 of 9) — heavy skew makes rungs harder to separate, so elimination is weaker.

hyperedges.label: The three venue panels form one small-multiple result
The figure's honesty argument: retained set over ranking, median+IQR over mean
